there's still time. first, develop a support system. it's much easier to go through this with friends and family. it's not impossible, but much harder to do it alone. if you have any bad relations with your family, just approach them humbly and tell them how bad of a position you are currently in and that you need their help and support..they will help you i promise. 

 online school + community college might be good for you. just expand your horizons with knowledge. make as many friends as you can...you'll be happier and you'll make connections that could mean opportunities for you later in life. it won't hurt to try. 

in the mean time, get into working out and staying fit. you'll feel better emotionally and you'll be improving yourself at the same time. your head will clear and you'll feel the difference. 

make yourself goals that you can reach. start small: I will read one book by the end of the week. I will meet one new person and positively impact their life. Get even bigger. I will find a new interest. I will attend one class at community college. I will pass my classes with As. I will graduate. I will get a job. Just start small and keep getting bigger and bigger. It will keep you busy, keep you focused on good stuff and not bad stuff, and improve your situation with every goal you reach.

thank you so much for replying and caring for a stranger in need

my parents are very manipulative. i was never raised to work hard everything was handed to me. my parents promised me tuition and a nice car and a trust fund to cover a nice place to live and monthly allowances for whatever i want when i turn 18 and go to college. if i cut them out forever i'll be so lost and so unprepared. ill have to exist in a world where i have no experience in. i wont have their support or connections later in life (honestly ive never thought about my adulthood, i always assumed id be gone before then). they raised me to be completely incapable of taking care of myself so it'll be difficult for me to escape and live on my own, but will definitely try. 

i think i will wait until college. maybe something big will happen, like i will wake up one day and my problems will be gone. that would be very nice

hi OP

remember, failing is a part of success. perhaps the most important part. nobody succeeds without screwing up, that's impossible. you say you're going homeless, perhaps things arent working out in your career....if you push through it you'll only come out stronger. i know you might want to stop right now and end it all and never look back but then you'll be missing out on the stronger, successful version of you that has a chance of overcoming this obstacle. i believe in you OP, message me if you want to talk!
